standard.title: Food characteristics and healthy eating
standard.description: Explain how the characteristics of foods influence selection and preparation for healthy eating
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can describe the ways food can be selected and prepared for healthy eating (AC9TDE4K04). They understand that food choices affect health. They have not yet explained how specific food characteristics (nutritional value, spoilage, preparation requirements, taste) drive selection and preparation decisions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how the characteristics of foods — nutritional value, spoilage, preparation requirements, taste — influence selection and preparation decisions for healthy eating.

nodes.label: Food characteristics that influence selection
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explain how food characteristics — nutritional value, availability, spoilage, taste — influence which foods are selected for healthy eating
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two food characteristics and explain how each influences whether a food is selected for a healthy meal
nodes.typical_width: Explain how nutritional value, availability, spoilage risk, preparation requirements and taste each influence food selection; apply the Australian Dietary Guidelines to plan a healthy meal or lunchbox for a specific individual — explaining selection decisions in terms of food characteristics
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australians have long selected foods based on nutritional value, seasonal availability, spoilage characteristics, and preparation requirements — exploring how this knowledge guided sustainable food choices over generations
Explore how flavour profiles (sour, salty, sweet, spicy, umami — particularly from Asian cuisines) influence food selection and preparation preferences across different cultural groups
Investigate how food service options at a local restaurant or café reflect food characteristic trade-offs — identifying how chefs balance nutrition, taste, availability and spoilage in menu design

response_modes.reason: Students tend to select foods based on taste preference and treat healthy eating as a rule set rather than a characteristic-based reasoning process. Multiple contexts — cultural traditions, dietary guidelines, food service — help students see food selection as applying a set of criteria to characteristics, not following a prescribed list.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The First Nations food selection context is rich — it presents characteristic-based selection as a long-standing, systematically developed knowledge rather than modern nutrition science alone. The cross-cultural flavour context is also rich for building understanding of how taste characteristics vary by cultural context.
success_criteria: Names at least two food characteristics
Explains how each characteristic influences whether a food is selected for healthy eating
nodes.hinge_reason: Food selection reasoning in N1 cascades directly into N2 — if students cannot identify characteristics (spoilage risk, nutritional value) as the basis for selection, they cannot connect those same characteristics to preparation decisions. The two nodes share the same conceptual structure.

nodes.label: Food characteristics that influence preparation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how food characteristics influence preparation methods and techniques
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one food and explain how its characteristics (e.g. spoilage risk, texture, nutritional content) determine how it should be prepared
nodes.typical_width: Explain how different food characteristics — perishability, hygiene requirements, nutritional value, texture — determine preparation methods; apply this understanding to design a food product or meal that meets health and safety requirements
wider: Experiment with preservation techniques (pickling, fermentation, air drying, sun drying) and explain how each technique responds to specific food characteristics — connecting the preservation method to the characteristic being managed

Investigate work practices that reflect nutrition, hygiene and food safety considerations — explaining how washing produce, safe oil disposal, refrigeration of perishables, and allergen awareness each respond to a specific food characteristic
Explore the food service skills needed to prepare food for healthy eating in a restaurant or café context — identifying how preparation techniques vary with the food's characteristics

response_modes.reason: Students commonly follow preparation steps without connecting them to the food's characteristics. The reasoning chain — what characteristic does this food have? → what preparation risk or opportunity does that create? → what technique responds to it? — makes preparation decisions principled rather than procedural.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one food characteristic that determines how a food must be prepared
Explains the connection between the characteristic and the preparation method
